topic: What frequency planning challenges arise when coordinating multiple ground stations with overlapping satellite visibility windows?
response: Overlap in satellite visibility windows creates interference challenges due to both NGSO and GSO satellites potentially operating on the same frequency.  This can lead to in-line interference between LEO satellites, especially when beams cross the equator line and operate in the same frequency. Effective coordination is crucial for mitigating this interference.
reference_context: The increasing number of satellites in LEO occupying amateur radio spectrum together with variety of modulation techniques, data rates and protocols used across the cubesat community demands the integration of a multitude of communication standards onto a single platform.
